newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The second Test, beginning in Sydney on Friday, will be short of Steve Waugh following a groin strain which has ruled him out of the clash against the West Indies. Waugh hopes to return for a one-day match on Melbourne on December 13 so he can test his finess for Australia's one-day international against Pakistan in Adelaide later next month. Page 20.

A teary Karrie Webb paid tribute to her wheelchair-bound coach, Kelvin Haller, after winning the A$865,270 U.S. LPGA Tour Championship in Las Vegas yesterday. The 21-year-old Australian, who began playing 13 years ago, has become the first player in LPGA tour history to top the US$1 million mark in a single season. Page 20.

Basketball Australia is expected to reappoint head coaches Barry Barnes and Tom Maher for the national positions at a board meeting today. Barnes took the Australian Boomers to fourth place, while Maher's Opals took out bronze at the Olympic Games in Atlanta this year. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Greg Norman will finally sever his links with the International Management Group at the end of this week's A$700,000 Greg Norman Holden Classic at Royal Melbourne. From the early 1980s, Norman has been slowly dismantling his relationship with IMG after chosing to handle his own management affairs with the formation of the suitably titled Great White Shark Enterprises. Page 50.

With one day remaining in the first Test of Australia vs West Indies at Brisbane, Australia faces the task of taking nine wickets within 90 overs. Australia declared at 6-217, setting the West Indies 420 runs to win off a minimum 119 overs. The visitors wre 1-89 at stumps yesterday. Page 50.

In front of 10,000 of Limerick's most uncompromising rugby union fans in Ireland, Australia will try to claim victory against Munster - rugby union's answer to the ultimate international giant killers. Former Australian coach Bob Dwyer describes Munster a "aggressive, physical, knock 'em down, jump on them type players". Munster has defeated Australia on three occasions in '67, '82 and most recently in 1992. Page 49.
THE AGE

The cricket test between Australia and the West Indies in Brisbane may hinge on a tussle today between arguably the world's best batsman and bowler -- Brian Lara and Shane Warne. Warne has dismissed Lara only once in Test cricket, and rarely has Warne had s many runs behind him. The West Indies chase 420 in a minimum of 119 overs. Page C8.

Melbourne Cup winner Saintly is responding well to treatment for the travel sickness that caused his shock scratching from Sunday's Japan Cup. A spokesman for trainer Bart Cummings said the horse's progress will be closely monitored before the long return trip to Australia. Page C7.

A report into the media coverage of females in sport released yesterday by Womensport Australia found female Olympians appeared on the front pages of Australian newspapers far more often than their male counter parts. The report also declared media coverge of women's sport at the Atlanta Games was "fair, neutral and even". Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

The West Indies' powerful batsman Brian Lara will attempt to defy expectations and lead a win for his team's target of 420 against Australia in the first Test at the Gabba today. Lara, who holds records for the highest Test (375) and first class (501 N.O.) scores has already indicated he will not let the West Indies go down after yesterday scoring 25 in just four overs before stumps. Page 72.

Australian Football League stalwarts Collingwood have asked the AFL to schedule up to nine of its home games a year at Victoria Park rather than the MCG. Club president Kevin Rose said it was increasingly difficult for the Magpies to draw 65,000 to matches at the MCG to break even. Page 70.

Queensland golfer Karrie Webb paid an emotional tribute to her wheelchair bound coach yesterday after taking out the U.S. LPGA Tour championship in Las Vegas. Webb, 21, burst into tears as she thanked Kelvin Haller for fixing several flaws in her game. Page 66.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian golfing ace Karrie Webb hit the jackpot by winning the season-ending U.S. LPGA Tour Champion. Webb's four-stroke victory took her year's earnings to A$1,233,963. Despite the windfall, a teary-eyed Webb insisted that her win went out to her wheelchair-bound coach, Kelvin Haller. Page 64.

Australia's new national soccer coach, Terry Venables, said he was offered over A$400,000 in a one-year contract to remain England's coach. However Venables remained dissatisfied with the offer, claiming the security of his position would have remained. The England FA offer was later withdrawn leaving Venables to believe "they didn't want me". Page 62.

The clash in Limerick between the Australian Wallabies and Ireland's Munster has been billed as rugby union war. While the Wallabies' scars of four years ago are yet to heal, when they were beaten 22-19, the game is tipped to produce more punches than points. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
